title: ACECODER: Acing Coder RL via Automated Test-Case Synthesis
data_curation: ACECODER builds ACECODE-87K through a fully automated test-case synthesis pipeline. Seeds are Magicoder-Evol-Instruct-110K, Magicoder-OSS-Instruct-75K, and bigcode/stack-dedup-python-fns; only Python questions containing a function or class are kept (124K entries). GPT-4o-mini rewrites each (question, solution) pair into a refined LeetCode-style question and imagines ~20 test cases; the original program solutions are discarded and used only as seeds. Test-case filtering uses Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct as a proxy: it generates a reference program per question, and any test the proxy fails is removed; questions with fewer than 5 surviving tests are dropped. This yields 87.1K questions and 1.38M cleaned tests. A human study of 200 sampled tests found only 3 invalid. For RM training, 16 programs are sampled per question from Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, and pairs are kept only when 1[si>sj+0.4, si>0.8, sj>0], yielding ~300K on-policy preference pairs from 46,618 questions.
curriculum: The training flows as: seed data -> automated test-case synthesis and filtering (ACECODE-87K) -> on-policy preference-pair construction -> reward-model fine-tuning (ACECODE-RM-7B/32B) -> Best-of-N inference or RL. RL is run from three initial policies (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Base, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct) with two reward types (learned RM and rule-based binary pass rate), giving six models. Echoing DeepSeek-R1/DeepSeek-Zero, the authors also perform RL directly from Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Base without SFT, arguing SFT can trap the policy in a local minimum; coding is treated as a verifiable task like math. RL uses a subsampled 'hard' slice (the 25% of questions with lower average pass rate and higher variance) so sampled programs stay diverse and informative. No multi-stage SFT->RL curriculum or cross-stage warmup/anneal schedule is described.
method: The core contribution is automated large-scale test-case synthesis that supplies reliable reward signals for code, enabling both a coding reward model and RL. The reward model uses a Bradley-Terry pairwise loss L(phi) = -1/(n(n-1)) sum sum 1[si>sj] log sigma(R_phi(x,yi)-R_phi(x,yj)), where scores si are test-case pass rates; the RM is a fully fine-tuned instruct coder with a linear head over the last token's hidden state. For RL the paper formalizes PPO but adopts Reinforcement++ (Hu, 2025), which drops the value model and computes advantage from RM rewards and per-token KL, reporting better efficiency and stability than PPO/GRPO. Rewards are either the learned ACECODE-RM-7B or a rule-based binary pass rate (1 iff all tests pass), mirroring Tulu3/DeepSeek-R1 verifiable rewards. Training uses OpenRLHF (rollout batch 256, 8 samples/question, LR 5e-7, 1 episode, 8xH100 in 6h). Ablations confirm test-case filtering and a Qwen (vs Llama) coder backbone both materially help.
eval_metrics: Evaluation spans HumanEval(+), MBPP(+), BigCodeBench (completion/instruct, full/hard), and LiveCodeBench (V4), with pass@1 (greedy), average over samples, and oracle pass@N; Best-of-N selects the highest-RM-scoring sample (top-p, temp 1.0, N=16/32/64). Reward models are also scored on RM-Bench (Code/Chat/Math/Safety/Easy/Normal/Hard/Avg) and compared against RewardBench leaders. Headline numbers: ACECODE-RM-7B lifts Llama-3.1-8B-Ins by +8.4 avg (Best-of-N) and ACECODE-RM-32B by +10.7; the '7B+7B' pairing with Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Ins adds +2.6. ACECODE-RM-32B tops RM-Bench at 76.1 avg, leading Coding/Chat/Normal/Hard, and the 7B variant beats NVIDIA-Nemotron-340B-Reward by 7.5 on coding. RL from Qwen2.5-7B-Ins adds +2.1 avg; R1-style RL from Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Base with rule rewards yields +25% HumanEval-plus and +6% MBPP-plus in 80 steps (48 H100-h), and lifts BigCodeBench-Instruct-Full from 40.2 to 43.2, near DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B (43.9).
key_results: ACECODE-RM-7B boosts Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct by +8.4 avg (Best-of-N) and ACECODE-RM-32B by +10.7 across HumanEval/MBPP/BigCodeBench/LiveCodeBench; ACECODE-RM-32B tops RM-Bench at 76.1 avg, beating Nemotron-340B-Reward by 7.5 on coding. R1-style RL from Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Base with rule-based pass rewards gives +25% HumanEval-plus and +6% MBPP-plus in just 80 steps (48 H100 GPU-hours). ACECODER-Rule lifts BigCodeBench-Instruct-Full from 40.2 to 43.2, approaching DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B (43.9).
evolution_note: Building on DeepSeek-R1's verifiable-reward RL-from-base recipe, Tulu3/DeepSeekMath GRPO, and Magicoder's OSS-Instruct data synthesis, ACECODER reacts to the fact that general reward models (e.g., Skywork) fail on code due to missing test-grounded signals. By automating test-case synthesis at scale, it supplies the missing reward signal and motivates later code-RL work showing that very short RL runs from a base coder can rival distilled reasoning models.
